title: 大风卷走座位表  (A Sudden Gust of Wind)

segments.t: The instant Zhou steps into the open courtyard with his giant white poster, a lively afternoon wind sweeps straight through the front gate. Qing and Peng sprint across the flagstones to help. Listen to the whole scene first.
哇！我的座位图怎么像大海上的帆船一样直往外拽？！
周经理，快捏紧下面两个角——刚从拱门灌进来一阵大风！
快抬头看！第一条绳上的纸灯笼正缠着第二条打转呢！
糟了，眼镜从额头上滑下来了——我腾出一只手扶一下！
周经理，千万别松开纸右边那个角！
呼——第一桌到第七桌快回来！别往院子树那儿飞呀！
在草药花盆那儿差点儿抓住了——小心，它又乘上第二阵风了！
它飘过第四桌，往左一拐，直奔院子里的石水盆去了！
千万别掉进石水盆！那可是水溶蓝墨水，不是防水漆呀！
小晴，往左扑过去！趁它还没脸朝下砸进水里，快拽住干的那一角！
哗啦……不偏不倚落进水盆正中央，像只大白纸船。
你们俩快告诉我这是做梦——药师和面包师的名字跑哪儿去了？！
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
哇！我的座位图怎么像大海上的帆船一样直往外拽？！
'Whoa! Why is my seating chart tugging like a sailboat out on the open sea?!' "Zhi" before an action word ("zhi wang wai zhuai") expresses continuous force—"tugging straight outward" with no letup.
周经理，快捏紧下面两个角——刚从拱门灌进来一阵大风！

'Pinch both bottom corners tight, Zhou—a huge gust just poured through the arch!' "Niejin" means pinching and holding tight with your fingers, while "guan jinlai" pictures wind rushing in as if through a funnel.
快抬头看！第一条绳上的纸灯笼正缠着第二条打转呢！

'Look up! Line one of the paper lanterns is tangling and spinning around line two!' "Taitou" combines "lift" + "head" to say "look up," and "chanzhe ... dazhuan" describes one cord coiling and spinning around the other.
糟了，眼镜从额头上滑下来了——我腾出一只手扶一下！

'Oh no, my glasses are slipping off my forehead—let me free one hand to catch them!' "Tengchu yi zhi shou" literally means "clear out one hand" to free it up, and "fu yixia" is a quick, gentle grab to steady something.
周经理，千万别松开纸右边那个角！
'Zhou, whatever you do, don't let go of that right corner of the paper!' "Qianwan bie" raises an urgent warning ("by all means, never..."), and "songkai" means to loosen your grip and let go.
呼——第一桌到第七桌快回来！别往院子树那儿飞呀！

'Whoosh—Tables One through Seven, come right back! Stop flying toward the courtyard tree!' Stretching "hu" mimics the whoosh of paper lifting off, while "wang ... fei" tracks the chart flying straight toward the tree.
在草药花盆那儿差点儿抓住了——小心，它又乘上第二阵风了！

'I almost caught it by the herb pots—watch out, it just caught a second breeze!' "Chadianr" means "almost" or "by a hair," and "chengshang" pictures the poster riding a wave of wind like catching a ride.
它飘过第四桌，往左一拐，直奔院子里的石水盆去了！

'It's gliding past table four, banking left, and heading straight for the courtyard stone basin!' "Wang zuo yi guai" captures a sudden sharp turn to the left, while "zhiben" means charging directly toward a target.
千万别掉进石水盆！那可是水溶蓝墨水，不是防水漆呀！

'Not into the stone water basin! That's water-soluble blue ink, not waterproof paint!' Contrasting "shuirong" ("water-dissolving") with "fangshui" ("water-blocking," waterproof) clearly explains why Zhou panics.
小晴，往左扑过去！趁它还没脸朝下砸进水里，快拽住干的那一角！
'Dive left, Qing! Grab the dry corner before it slams face down into the water!' "Puguoqu" means lunging or diving across, while "chen" + "hai mei" literally urges action before it hits the water.
哗啦……不偏不倚落进水盆正中央，像只大白纸船。
'Splash... right into the exact center of the basin like a big white paper boat.' Qing uses "huala" to capture the splash, and four-character "bupian" + "buyi" literally means dead center.
你们俩快告诉我这是做梦——药师和面包师的名字跑哪儿去了？！

'Tell me I'm dreaming, you two—where did the pharmacist and the baker run off to?!' Adding "shi" ("master" or skilled specialist) creates professions like "yaoshi" (pharmacist) and "mianbaoshi" (baker).
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.

周经理，快捏紧下面两个角——刚从拱门灌进来一阵大风！

呼——第一桌到第七桌快回来！别往院子树那儿飞呀！
在草药花盆那儿差点儿抓住了——小心，它又乘上第二阵风了！
它飘过第四桌，往左一拐，直奔院子里的石水盆去了！
千万别掉进石水盆！那可是水溶蓝墨水，不是防水漆呀！
小晴，往左扑过去！趁它还没脸朝下砸进水里，快拽住干的那一角！
哗啦……不偏不倚落进水盆正中央，像只大白纸船。
你们俩快告诉我这是做梦——药师和面包师的名字跑哪儿去了？！
One gust of wind tangles the rooftop lanterns above and lands twenty-eight blue ink names squarely in the courtyard water basin! See you next time.
再见！
